info.title: Turvo API
info.description:
OAS Spec document outlining Turvo external APIs

Customer Action Required: New Public API Enhancement

On November 30, 2023, a new enhancement to our Public API designed to provide enhanced security and improve API call management will be a requirement to use our Public API. This is a mandatory update for all customers using our Public API. All Turvo integrations using the Public API will be impacted by this enhancement. To learn how to generate your API key in Turvo to use this API enhancement, see the API Key Management article in the Help Center. For any questions or concerns, contact your Turvo representative.

tags.name: API Overview
tags.description: Turvo is the only real-time collaborative logistics platform that connects anyone, anywhere to move things.Turvo creates a smarter way for shippers, brokers, and carriers to seamlessly work together to get things done faster. Turvo API provides you with the ability to integrate with Turvo through [RESTful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer#RESTful_web_services) methods. Our API has predictable, resource-oriented URLs, and uses HTTP response codes to indicate API errors. All requests and responses are in [JSON](https://www.json.org/) format. Turvo’s entities are document oriented: they can have fairly deeply nested sets of attributes. For example, a shipment contains two significant sub-objects : a customerOrder and a carrierOrder. These sub-objects themselves have a significant number of properties. Turvo’s systems allow for `partial updates` of each entity: for an update the entire entity data does not need to be sent over, in fact, such an operation is discouraged as it can potentially overwrite a concurrent update to the same entity.As an example, if one wants to simply modify the customerOrder of a shipment, they should only send the customerOrder object as a part of an update [PUT] request. Any two concurrent updates that update different attributes of the same object will not result in a data conflict. Objects within arrays such as a customerOrder require metadata when operated on: we need to distinguish whether an object is added to an array, deleted from an array, or updated.For example, when updating a customerOrder in a shipment, the client must specify the `customerOrder.id` as a part of the update. This pattern applies for all entities within Turvo. * We achieve this by using the `_operation` attribute, which can be set to either `0`, `1`, or `2`. * Along with the `_operation` key/value, we also require that you specify the corresponding identifier of the sub-object. * When set to `0`, we insert the object in the array; * When set to `1` we update the object in the array; * When set to `2` the object is removed from the array; * For operations `1` and `2` the identifier of the sub-object is required, for operation `0` no identifier should be set. Objects within arrays are `soft-deleted`, and clients need to be able to handle elements which are flagged as deleted. Such objects will have a `deleted` attribute and the value of that attribute will be set to `true`. Turvo utilizes a special type of enumeration called a Lookup. Lookups contain a key (which is effectively a fixed code) and a display value. These are required for a variety of attributes in the API: one example would be the the equipment type. When setting lookup values, both the key and the value need to be set. Note: Refer to our API Quick Start Guide if you want to use our Public API right away.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
Security Scheme Type HTTP
HTTP Authorization Scheme bearer
The Turvo Public API supports authentication of your application API requests with its resources via the OAuth 2.0 (bearer token) authentication method.

Authentication API Details

The Authentication API is used to authenticate API requests and is required to authenticate Turvo Public API resources. Turvo provides a combination of Client ID (API Key) and Client Secret (Secret Key) to authenticate API requests for your project. Each project under your organization is associated with a combination of Client ID and Client Secret, called as API credentials.

How to get your Public API Credentials

  • For Client Id and Client Secret -> Please check admin console -> Public API Profiles section.
API credentials serve the following purposes of:
  • Identifying the project making a call to the APIs.
  • Authenticating access to the APIs that are enabled under your project.

How the Authentication API Works

API Authentication

Once you have obtained the API credentials, the OAuth endpoint is used to get an access token which is used as credentials with each API transaction. To access Turvo resources, use the following endpoints to authenticate your application in the sandbox and production environments respectively:
  • https://my-sandbox-publicapi.turvo.com/v1/oauth/token
  • https://publicapi.turvo.com/v1/oauth/token
Provide the following required query parameters: 
  client_id = *******

  client_secret = ******
Provide the following required headers: 
  x-api-key = "***********"
Note: API keys are generated within the Admin Console, specifically in the 'Api & Webhooks' card. The following required inputs associated with the OAuth request are: 
  "grant_type": "password",

  "username": "*********",

  "password": "**********",

  "scope": "read+trust+write",

  "type": "business"
Note: The field ‘scope’ will have permissions “read+trust+write”. The field ‘type’ can be anything but the default type is ‘business’. The response to this request includes the following:
  • access_token – The encrypted OAuth token that needs to be used in the API transaction.
  • token_type – Type of token. In this case, it is bearer authentication.
  • expires_in – Token expiration time in seconds. 12 hours is the standard Token expiration time.
  • Scope – Scope of authentication provided to the customer. In this case, it is “read+trust+write”.
For recurrent authentication API calls, the access token created in the first call will only be returned for reuse for the next 10 hours, with expires_in updated to the remaining time until it expires.
The fresh access token will be generated on the next authentication API call after 10 hours from the previous generation; however, an access token can be reused for 12 hours after it is created.
The optimum approach to utilize this authentication API is to call once and then use the access token for the next 12 hours. As soon as we receive a 401 Unauthorized (invalid_token) response, we should perform the next authentication API call to regenerate it.
Refresh tokens can be used for getting the new access token, by providing it in the OAuth request: 
     { "grant_type":"refresh_token", "refresh_token":"***********" }
Refresh token is valid for 30 days. On expiry of refresh token, re-authentication using credentials are required.

tags.name: Release Notes
tags.description:
This section features the new and enhanced API features and updates to the Public API. For detailed information on these features, check out the Release Notes on our Help Center.

Production API Docs

Turvo updates the production API documentation on the same day as its monthly production release.

My-Sandbox API Docs

Turvo updates the My-Sandbox API documentation about 10 days before the production release, during what's called the preview period. These updates will match what's eventually published in the production API docs.

Rehearsal API Docs

Turvo updates the Rehearsal API documentation approximately 17 days before the production release (or one week before the My-Sandbox release). Although customers don't have access to the Rehearsal environment, they can use these docs to get an early look at upcoming API changes. The same updates will appear later in the My-Sandbox and Production API documentation.

BREAKING CHANGE - Effective R2.2026

  • Location API - Phone Number Type Change: The phone.number field in Location Create and Update APIs has been changed from integer to string type. All location API calls must be compliant with the new contract by R2.2026. Please update your integrations to send phone numbers as strings.
  • Location API - Contract Validation: All payloads coming to Location Create and Update will be validated against the contract and will fail in case of non-compliance. Non-compliant requests will be rejected after R2.2026.

09/24/2025

  • We've enhanced the Carrier Filtering API to support case-insensitive filtering by existing taxId field. This improvement allows users to filter carriers regardless of letter casing in the taxId field.
  • We've enhanced the locations filtering API to support filtering by additional location attributes, this will be helpful for users to filter locations based on their specific needs.

09/02/2025

  • In this release, we've introduced a new "Interline" lookup in the Shipment lookup section. This is helpful for users to update shipment status to interline for LTL Mode.
  • In this release, we've introduced new fields "state, countryCode, countryName" in Shipment status update and Shipment retrieve call.

07/30/2025

  • We've added a new webhook event 'EXCEPTION_RESOLVED' for Exception.
  • We've added a new field 'shipmentLength' in equipment section. This will be helpful for users if someone wants to define shipment length in equipment.
  • In this release, we've introduced a new "serviceArea" field within the carrierOrder section of the Retrieve Shipment public API and the SHIPMENT_UPDATE webhooks. This enhancement enables users to access assigned LTL carrier service area details directly through the API and webhooks. Additionally, the Shipments List API now supports filtering shipments by "serviceAreaKey" via query parameters. We have also added serviceAreas lookup values in the Shipment lookup section.

07/02/2025

  • In SHIPMENT_UPDATE Webhook, when carrier is removed from a shipment, the 'dotNo' was sometimes being sent as String although it was expected to be Integer, this has been fixed.
  • Filter Shipment API - added deleted flag for each customer order and carrier order
  • We have added carrier lanes information to the Carrier Add/Update webhook and public API. This enhancement allows customers to access and manage carrier lane data through both webhooks and API endpoints. The following fields are now available
    • lanes.origin - Origin location details including
      • line1, line2, line3 (string)
      • city.name, state.name (string)
      • zip (integer)
      • country.name, country.code (string)
      • gps.coordinates (array of float)
    • lanes.destination - Destination location details including
      • line1, line2, line3 (string)
      • city.name, state.name (string)
      • zip (integer)
      • country.name, country.code (string)
      • gps.coordinates (array of float)
    • lanes.type - Type information with key and value
    • lanes.rateQualifier - Rate qualifier information with key and value
    • lanes.price (float) - Price for the lane
    • lanes.priority - Priority information with key and value

06/04/2025

  • Introduced equipment services related fields to SHIPMENT_ADD/SHIPMENT_UPDATE webhook:
    • servicesNote (string)
    • servicesPartial (boolean)
  • Equipment services fields are also added in the Retrieve a Shipment/GET Shipment
    • details.servicesNote (string)
    • details.servicesPartial (boolean)
  • Introduced carrier and customer order related fields to SHIPMENT_STATUS_UPDATE webhook
    • carrierOrder.deleted (boolean)
    • carrierOrder.id (Turvo ID of the carrier order) (String)
    • carrierOrder.carrier.id (Turvo ID of the carrier) (String)
    • customerOrder.deleted(boolean)
    • customerOrder.id (Turvo ID of the customer order) (String)
    • customerOrder.customer.id (Turvo ID of the customer)(String)
  • In this release, we've introduced a new 'parent' object to the customerOrder items in the create/update Shipment public API. This enhancement enables users to define mix-pallet items by establishing parent-child relationships between items.

05/07/2025

  • We have added the ability to filter shipments by customer id in shipment list api.
  • In public API response for SHIPMENT create/update/retrieve. We would be returning additional fields which will be helpful to map user key/sourceid (globalShipLocationSourceId) and turvo generated id(globalShipLocationId) for route locations. Below fields are added to the response
    • details -> globalRoute -> globalShipLocationSourceId
    • details -> customerOrder -> route -> globalShipLocationId
    • details -> customerOrder -> route -> globalShipLocationSourceId
    • details -> customerOrder -> items -> pickupLocation -> globalShipLocationSourceId (It was already part of response schema documentation, but not getting returned in actual response)
    • details -> customerOrder -> items -> deliveryLocation -> globalShipLocationSourceId (It was already part of response schema documentation, but not getting returned in actual response)
  • Added 'details -> globalRoute -> address' and 'details -> customerOrder -> route -> address -> country' in response of Shipment Retrieve public API.
  • Added new public-api endpoints to create and update documents via signed url. Please refer 'API SERVICES -> Documents -> Create Document via signed URL' and 'API SERVICES -> Documents -> Update a document via signed URL' sections for the request/response structure.
  • Added 'details -> file -> id' and 'details -> file -> url' in response of Fetch details of a document public API.
  • In public API documentation for SHIPMENT create/update, we have updated documentation to add equipment for carrier orders.

04/09/2025

  • We have added the ability to filter users by email, ignoring case sensitivity in user list api.
  • Added new USER_DELETE webhook which can be subscribed to from Admin console.
  • Added new webhook events for CUSTOMER_DELETE, CARRIER_DELETE and FACTOR_DELETE.
  • We’ve added the new fields 'createdBy' and 'updatedBy' to the Filter Exceptions API response. These fields indicate the user who initially created the exception and the user who last updated it.
  • We’ve added the fields IssueStatus, IssuePhase, and IssueDescription to the EXCEPTION_ADD/EXCEPTION_UPDATE webhook payload. These fields represent the exception's status, phase, and description added on the exception. Additionally, we’ve replaced the TurvoShipmentId field with the Entity object, which includes EntityId and EntityType to specify to which entity (shipment/order/inventory) the exception was linked.

03/12/2025

  • In this release, we've added a "quoteId" field in Retrieve Shipment public API call. The quoteId parameter will only be retrieved in case of quoted shipments.
  • In this release, we've added an "reasonCode" field to the SHIPMENT_UPDATE and SHIPMENT_STATUS_UPDATE webhook. With this enhancement, we'll be able to share the reasons with customers when Shipment Status and Appointment Schedules are manually updated in Turvo. Further, the reason code can be updated via public API and can be retrieved through public API call.
  • Added "shipmentStatusHistory" field in Retrieve Shipment public API call. This enhancement enables user to keep a track of status update history of a shipment.

02/12/2025

  • Removed 'sortOrder', 'default' fields from DOCUMENT_SAVED webhook as they were internal
  • Removed 'sortOrder' and 'defaults' fields from SHIPMENT_ADD/SHIPMENT_UPDATE webhook as they are internal fields.
  • We’ve added a new field 'isDefaultViewable' to the GET User API response. This boolean flag indicates whether the group is set as default view for the user or not.
  • We’ve have exposed default group in GET Group list api response. To retrieve the default group, include the parameter getDefaultGroup=true in your GET Group List API request. The default group will be included in the response, based on the specified page size.
  • In this release, we've corrected the spelling of commission recipients in the Shipment (SHIPMENT_ADD/SHIPMENT_UPDATE), Customer (CUSTOMER_ADD/CUSTOMER_UPDATE) and Document (DOCUMENT_ADD/DOCUMENT_UPDATE) webhooks. Initially it was spelled like "comissions" and now we have updated to "commission". We have done this to make it sync with public API payloads.
  • In this release, we've added a "rateType" field to the carrierOrder cost section in both the Retrieve Shipment public API and the SHIPMENT_UPDATE webhooks. This enhancement allows users to determine whether the assigned LTL carrier rate is a CSP rate or not via the API and webhooks.

12/11/2024

  • Shipment Create and Update can be used to control auto sending of rate confirmation to carriers. This was earlier missing in the API documentation and now has been added as part of this release.
  • New fields have been added in Item master, Shipment and Order Items to enhance an item's stacking information. New fields include stackDimensionsLimit, loadBearingCapacity and maxStackCount.

11/13/2024

  • In this release, we've introduced a "referenceNo" field inside customerOrder/carrierOrder payment section in the Shipment for (Shipment Create/Update/Retrieve) public api and (SHIPMENT_ADD/SHIPMENT_UPDATE) webhooks. This fix allows users to track payment "referenceNo" in the shipments through public Api and webhooks.
  • We have introduced id, and value fields along with key in the accounts( customer, carrier, and factor) status.code model representing the account status
  • We have introduced a new field called "id" at the path paymentTerm.id in the request payload for the Update Carrier API which was missing in documentation. Additionally, we've enhanced the paymentTerm object with detailed field descriptions related to carrier advances. Furthermore, we have added lookup keys under the LOOKUPS -> Carrier section for PayTermType and included the previously missing PaymentType lookup keys.

10/16/2024

  • In this release, we've introduced a new "deleted" flag for commission recipients in the Shipment (SHIPMENT_ADD/SHIPMENT_UPDATE) and Customer (CUSTOMER_ADD/CUSTOMER_UPDATE) webhooks. This fix allows users to easily identify and track commission recipients who have been deleted from shipments, providing better data clarity and management of commission records.
  • We have updated the API documentation with lookup keys under LOOKUPS -> Document section corresponding to DocumentStatus for all applicable document types supported on Public API on Turvo.
  • We have added a new field named "key" at the path `paymentTerm.method` in the request payload of `Update Carrier API`. This field is required when adding payment terms onto carrier accounts. Value of the field "key" should represent a lookup key under LOOKUPS -> Carrier section corresponding to a PaymentType.
  • We have updated the API documentation with the lookup key under LOOKUPS -> Shipment section corresponding to CostType `Accessorial - Other`.

09/18/2024

  • Turvo API now has validations for the account Status fields key when creating customer, carrier, or factor accounts via Public API. Only valid account status keys listed in the Lookups section per account type of Turvo API Documentation are accepted when making an API call to create the account. If an invalid key is identified, an error is raised.

10/12/2022

  • Turvo API now supports Reservations for Appointment Scheduling

10/20/2022

  • Turvo API now supports API Gateway Key Retrieval and Regeneration

07/21/2022

  • Turvo API now supports Appointments scheduling

03/10/2022

  • Turvo Shipments api now supports drayage specific attributes such as ETA at terminal, last free day and milestones from Telematics providers

02/17/2022

  • In Webhook Location_ADD and Location_Update gps and Geofence values are added

01/13/2022

  • In Turvo Contacts context.type value is changed CUSTOMER to SHIPPER for Customer account and FACTOR to FACTORING for Factor Account

01/13/2022

  • Turvo API now supports Parent account or Other account entity and related features.

12/12/2021

  • Turvo Cost types supports new type Other - Claim Expense

11/04/2021

  • Turvo Shipments API now supports mode specific attributes such as container number, vessel IMO number, tracking number, etc. for Ocean, Rail, Intermodal, LTL, and Parcel modes

09/30/2021

  • Turvo Shipments API now supports feasibility of adding and updating planned appointment dates of global route for a particular shipment

08/06/2021

  • Turvo Shipments API now supports Users to be designated on the shipment with a particular role like Broker, Operator, Dispatcher, Accounting

07/15/2021

  • Turvo Shipments API now supports filtering shipment by status, locationId, PickupDateRange, DeliverydDateRange, PO#, BOL#, Route#, Container#, TruckId etc

06/24/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Exceptions

06/17/2021

  • Turvo Location API now has receiveTurvoLinks in the phone

06/03/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Offers service

06/03/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Pallets service

06/03/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Inventory Summary service

05/27/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Inventory service

04/22/2021

  • Addition of Task lookups and mandatory fields to create a task

03/18/2021

  • Turvo Orders API now supports filtering order by created, updated, id, customId, status, PO#, Reference#, BOL# etc
  • Turvo Assets, Groups and Items API now supports filtering and pagination

02/25/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Items service

02/18/2021

  • Turvo shipment API now supports local date time on shipment status update

02/04/2021

  • Turvo Users API now supports filtering users by created, updated, email

01/28/2021

  • Turvo API now have filtering and pagination on the following api's.
    • users
    • locations
    • customers
    • carriers
    • factors
    • contacts
    • shipments
  • Groups and Payments info are now available in Shipments.

01/22/2021

  • Turvo API now provides Assets service
  • Associate an entity to Tags

12/17/2020

  • Flex Attributes are available in Orders.
  • Phone is no longer a required attribute in Users.

09/02/2020

  • Account Distribution, External Ids and Third Party Billing are available in Customers.
  • Billing is no longer available in Customers and is replaced by Third Party Billing.

08/26/2020

  • Shipments now includes Flex Attributes in customer and carrier orders.

08/15/2020

  • Groups are now available in the Users.
  • Permission id no longer needed in the Users.
  • User name and title are removed from Groups.
  • Account, Company, Geofence, Delivery Link, Dwell Time, External Ids and ware are now available in Locations.
To review archived API release notes from 2022 and older, see the Archived API Release Notes article in the Help Center

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Users API allows you to provide Turvo access to a new user, and specify relevant information about the user, such as name, permission, and contact information. In addition, it allows you to update information related to an existing user or permanently remove a user from Turvo.

tags.name: Parent Or Other Accounts
tags.description: Parent API allows you to do the logical grouping of entities. Also it provides with the seraching ability of entities like Shipment,Orders,Location etc. based on associated Parent account. Other Account object represents accounts you are providing service for, and allows you to store information about those accounts

tags.name: Groups
tags.description: Groups object enables you to create a collection of Users that belong to the same functional area. You can manage groups through the API, such as creating new groups, adding users to existing groups, or removing an existing group.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description: In Turvo, Location objects hold information relevant to the locations that your business interacts with. You can create new location, edit attributes of an existing location (such as hours of operation, contact information, and special instructions), and delete unused locations.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Customers object represents accounts you are providing service for, and allows you to store information about those accounts. Once created, you can use the customer reference across other Turvo entities, such as shipments.

tags.name: Factors
tags.description: Factors are accounts that purchase accounts receivables from carriers and helps them with cash flow. Factors object can store relevant information, such as contact info, and can be managed through the API.

tags.name: Carriers
tags.description: Carriers are accounts that perform the shipments for your company. In the Carriers object, you can track information relevant to specific carriers, such as SCAC, address, and DOT number.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: In Contacts object, you can store information about external people that your company interacts with. You can add information such as email and phone, and you can associate contacts to existing accounts or locations. Additionally, you can retrieve information about a contact using their ID, edit them, or delete them from Turvo.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: In Assets object, you can store vehicle information, sensor and carrier details. You can track the assets using Turvo or Geotab devices.

tags.name: Items
tags.description: Item object represents a product and relevant information of the product. An item can be added to shipment and/or order based on the inventory.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: control the inflow and outflow of inventory by facility and at a lot level.

tags.name: Inventory 2.0
tags.description:
Inventory 2.0 is an extended version of Inventory with some additional features outlined below that represent extensible inventory data model, which can accommodate inventory ingested at the lowest (for example serial) level. It is backwards compatible with inventory. Using the Inventory 2.0, you can:
  • Send consolidated inventory data to Turvo through the API at the base record level to add, update, or delete inventory from a given record.
  • Update inventory quantities for a specific inventory record with a provided reason code to view what updates to inventory occur with corresponding reason code
  • Add, update, or delete multiple inventory records at any given time.
  • Receive inventory updates at any time as shipping can occur all through the night keeping your inventory records consistently in sync as items are picked, shipped, and received in the warehouse
  • Receive the unique IDs upon performing an add, update, or delete operation after a successful transaction keeping the outside systems cross-referenced if they need to perform further manipulation on the inventory record.
  • As an administrative user, you get timeline time stamps with details around inventory adjustments (and separate inventory quantity update messages) recorded so you can track down the time and date when a particular inventory adjustment occurs.

tags.name: Shipments
tags.description: Shipments object represents a unit of capacity that is being moved, and stores relevant information needed to move that unit of capacity. A shipment may have multiple customers, have specific start / end date, and serves specific route.

tags.name: LTL Quotes
tags.description: LTL (Less Than Truckload) API enables you to request shipping rates and book LTL shipments programmatically.

tags.name: Offers
tags.description: Offers allow Carrier or Customer to offer shipment with the specified amount.

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: Orders represents a delivery process used to move a product from its point of sale to the hands of the customer. It contains details about the type and quantity of items being ordered. It will also outline the cost that have been agreed upon.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: There are a number of instances in which you want to upload documents to Turvo, and associate them with other Turvo objects. For example, you may want to upload a Proof of delivery document and associate that to a shipment, or upload an Insurance document and associate that to a carrier. When you use Documents API to upload those documents, you need to provide the Turvo object associated with that document by using context.

tags.name: Settlements 2.0
tags.description: Settlements 2.0 API provides the capability to create and manage invoices in Turvo for your shipments

tags.name: Tags
tags.description: Tags are identifiable entities used across other Turvo objects that allow for quick retrieval of objects, classification, or workflow management. Tags can be created and attached to specific entities through the API.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: In Turvo, you can create a task and assign it to a Turvo user. Through the API, you can create new tasks and assign it to a user, as well as edit and view existing tasks.

tags.name: VIN
tags.description: Vehicle Identification Number [(VIN)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number) is a unique code used in the automotive industry to identify individual vehicles. Use this endpoint to retrieve detailed information of a vehicle, including make, model and dimensions.

tags.name: Exceptions
tags.description: Exceptions are used to communicate, track, and manage any unforeseen events that happen along a route that could affect the driver’s arrival time.

tags.name: Lookups
tags.description: Lookups are a flexible manner of defining enumerations within Turvo and are used throughout the system. Each lookup contains a key and a value. For each entity in Turvo you will see a list of lookups which are available. In the API you whenever you see a combination of a key/value, it refers to a Lookup (for example, for Customer -> phones -> type).

tags.name: Routing Guide
tags.description: RoutingGuides allow tendering shipments to carriers that have been pre-arranged to receive them based on set of rules defined.

tags.name: Reservations
tags.description: Reservations API provides the capability to create and manage slots and reservations in turvo appointment scheduling

tags.name: Appointments
tags.description: Appointments API provides the capability to create and manage appointments in turvo appointment scheduling

tags.name: Appointments 2.0
tags.description: Appointments 2.0 API provides the capability to create and manage appointments in turvo appointment scheduling

tags.name: API Gateway Key
tags.description: These public end points provides the capability to retrieve and regenerate API gateway key. API gateway keys are used to let public API calls go through the API Gateway to the internal services and is used as a request header ensuring valid access by forbidding unauthorized access.

tags.name: Tracking
tags.description: Provides a Public API to ingest location updates for tracking of shipments or assets .

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Turvo provides you with webhooks for a better integration between Turvo and your application. When your application needs to know and act upon certain events when they occur in your Turvo account such as an account being canceled or a payment that failed, you can use webhooks to notify your application. These include changes relating to accounts, locations, users, contacts, shipments and orders. Once you've configured the URL, Turvo will post the event to your webhook URL. For example, if a "SHIPMENT_UPDATE" event occurs, then a notification is sent to the specified URL. You can configure webhook alerts to keep track of any events relating to your shipments, orders, accounts, locations and contacts. The updates are push notifications that will be transferred to client endpoints on key triggers (or “Events”) in the turvo workflow. When a change occurs, the updates are sent as JSON objects to the predetermined callback URL provided by the client and should be processed by the receiving client according to this reference document. This makes updates more efficient, as you know exactly when a change has happened, and don't need to rely on continuous or even periodic requests when changes aren't happening. Webhook notifications are usually posted asynchronously and so are not recommended for time-critical applications. When time is critical, it is better to use the Turvo API. Handling Webhooks Turvo needs to get a status code 2XX reply from the configured URL to confirm that the notification sent via HTTP POST has been successfully delivered. If any webhook times out, Turvo will cancel and retry. Up to 3 retries happen for every webhook that fails and at 30 seconds time intervals. Versions
  • Webhooks V1.0
  • Webhooks V2.0
    • To know about each of the versions please refer the Webhook V1.0 and V2.0 section below.

tags.name: Events
tags.description:
Turvo introduces webhooks version 2.0. The new version is designed to handle updates as event notifications and will require to configure a single call back URL for multiple events. Any change that happens to the system is captured as an event with Webhooks V2.0. Here's a list of the event types supported in v2.0 that currently generates webhooks. All the events will contain the following fields
eventName The name of the entity that changed (ASSET_ADD, SHIPMENT_ADD, etc.)
tenantId The unique ID for your tenant in Turvo
eventTime The latest timestamp when the event occurred in UTC
eventPayload The event payload for the subscribed event. For each of the specific subscription refer the Webhooks v1.0 payload.

get.description:
Filter active locations by given parameters. Retrieve a list of locations based on various filter criteria including name, address, contact information, external IDs, tags, geographic coordinates, and timestamps.

**Supported Filter Parameters:**
- Location details: name, address (line1, city, state, zip, country code)
- Contact info: phone, email
- Classification: warehouse status, scheduling info, tags
- External IDs: account, CRM, ERP, project, contract, customer, location external IDs
- Geographic: GPS coordinates with radius
- Timestamps: creation and update dates

**Important:** Do NOT include explicit quotes in query parameter values. The quotes shown in examples are for documentation only and should not be included in actual API requests.

Example:
- ✅ Correct: `?name[eq]=Test Location`
- ❌ Wrong: `?name[eq]="Test Location"` (quotes become part of the value)

parameters.name: name[eq]
parameters.description: Location name to filter results. Supports only the "eq" operator (use square brackets after the field name).

parameters.name: line1Address[eq]
parameters.description: First line of the address to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: zip[eq]
parameters.description: Zip code of the address to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: city[eq]
parameters.description: City of the primary address to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: state[eq]
parameters.description: State of the primary address to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: countryCode[eq]
parameters.description: Country code of the primary address to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: isWarehouse[eq]
parameters.description: Indicates if the location is a warehouse. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: isSchedulingInfo[eq]
parameters.description: Indicates if scheduling is enabled for the location. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: accountId[eq]
parameters.description: Account ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: crmId[eq]
parameters.description: CRM ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: erpId[eq]
parameters.description: ERP ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: projectId[eq]
parameters.description: Project ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: contractId[eq]
parameters.description: Contract ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: other[eq]
parameters.description: Other identifier to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: region[eq]
parameters.description: Region ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: customerExternalId[eq]
parameters.description: Customer external ID to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: locationExternalId[eq]
parameters.description: Location external ID to filter results. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: tagName[eq]
parameters.description: Tag name to filter locations. Supports only the "eq" operator.

parameters.name: gps[in]
parameters.description: Filter locations by geographic coordinates. Supports only the "in" operator. Format is [longitude,latitude,radius]. Radius is in miles by default, with a maximum of 50 miles.

parameters.name: created[gte]
parameters.description: UTC timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the location was created. Supports the "gte" operator.

parameters.name: updated[lte]
parameters.description: UTC timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the location was last updated. Supports "eq", "in", "gte", and "lte" operators.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Index to start returning results from. For example, start=25 skips the first 25 records.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Number of records to return. For example, pageSize=10 returns up to 10 records, even if more match the criteria.

pagination.description: Pagination details containing next start, page size, number of records in current page, more records available

totalRecordsInPage.description: number of records in current page

moreAvailable.description: more records available with same criteria?

locations.description: locations matching given criteria. Only selected attributes will be returned in the response. To fetch the entire location document, please query the GET /locations/{id} endpoint

updated.description: location last updated date in ISO 8601 format

phones.description: List of phone numbers through which the location can be reached.

id.description:
Turvo ID for the markup profile.

Required when updating (_operation: 1) or deleting (_operation: 2) an existing markup profile.
Omit when creating a new markup profile (_operation: 0).

_operation.description:
Type of operation for the markup profile:
- 0: Insert (create new markup profile - do not provide id)
- 1: Update (modify existing markup profile - id is required)
- 2: Delete (remove existing markup profile - id is required)

name.description: Name of the markup profile. This is a user-defined name to identify the markup profile.

mode.description: Mode for the markup profile. Specify the transportation mode for this markup profile.

key.description: MarkupProfileMode key. Use "24107" for LTL or "24108" for FTL.

value.description: MarkupProfileMode value. Use "LTL" for Less Than Truckload or "FTL" for Full Truckload.

banyanReferenceId.description: Banyan reference ID for the markup profile. This is an external reference identifier for integration purposes.

id.description:
Turvo ID for the markup configuration.

Required when updating (_operation: 1) or deleting (_operation: 2) an existing markup configuration.
Omit when creating a new markup configuration (_operation: 0).

_operation.description:
Type of operation:
- 0: Insert (create new markup configuration - do not provide id)
- 1: Update (modify existing - id is required)
- 2: Delete (remove existing - id is required)

carriers.description: List of carriers for this markup configuration.

minimum.description:
Minimum value for the markup range (optional).
When specified, this markup configuration only applies when the total cost meets or exceeds this minimum value.
Leave null if no minimum threshold is needed.

maximum.description:
Maximum value for the markup range (optional).
When specified, this markup configuration only applies when the total cost is at or below this maximum value.
Leave null if no maximum threshold is needed.

markup.description: Markup details including value and type.

value.description:
Markup value.
- For Flat type: enter the fixed dollar amount (e.g., "123" means $123)
- For Percent type: enter the percentage (e.g., "23" means 23%)
- For Passthrough type: use 0 (no markup applied)

type.description:

name of the customer. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "eqi", "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand.

parameters.name: start

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Page size of the request to fetch number of records matching the criteria. For example, pageSize=10 will fetch only 10 records even if there are more than 10 matching results for the query.

parameters.name: status[eq]

post.description:
There are a number of things to consider while creating a carrier in Turvo -
  • Creating a carrier requires either a DOT number or an MC number to be specified
  • You can specify a number of payment methods to be associated with a carrier upon creation (and the payment methods need to have been defined in admin console). If the carrier is successfully created, the response will include a Turvo identifier for each payment method specified. You can then define the payment terms in a subsequent PUT request, and use the payment method identifier to associate specific payment methods to a payment term.

quote.description:
LTL quote information for booking. This is the complete quote object returned from GET /ltl/quotes/{quoteId}.

This field is used when booking an LTL shipment. It contains all the rating details including:
- Provider information (Banyan, P44, SMC3, Contract)
- Carrier details and capabilities
- Cost breakdown and line items
- Transit times and service levels
- Terminal information
- Facilitator and credential details

The quote object should be copied from the LTL quotes response and included here to preserve
all rating context and enable proper booking with the carrier.

These UUIDs identify the specific route segments/fragments that the carrier will service.
Typically these correspond to the shipment's global route segments.
For LTL bookings, this should match the routeFragmentId from the quote.

parameters.name: created[gte]
parameters.description: UTC datetime in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ format when the shipment was created.

parameters.name: updated[lte]
parameters.description: UTC datetime in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ format when the shipment was last updated. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "in", "gte", "lte". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, ?updated[gte]=2021-01-04T05:57:42Z

parameters.name: customId[eq]
parameters.description: customId of the shipment. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, customId[eq] or customId[in]

parameters.name: status[eq]
parameters.description: Status of the shipment. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, status[eq]=2101 or status[in]=[2101, 2102]

parameters.name: locationId[eq]
parameters.description: Location Id of the shipment. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, locationId[eq] or locationId[in]

parameters.name: pickupDate[gte]
parameters.description: Pickup date range of the shipment. Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, ?pickupDate[gte]=2021-07-22T00:00:00Z&pickupDate[lte]=2021-07-30T00:00:00Z

parameters.name: deliveryDate[lte]
parameters.description: Delivery date range of the shipment. Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, ?deliveryDate[gte]=2021-05-01T00:00:00Z&?deliveryDate[lte]=2021-07-01T00:00:00Z

parameters.name: customerId[eq]
parameters.description: Customer Id of the shipment. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, customerId[eq] or customerId[in]

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Start index of the next page to skip. For example, start=25 means skip the first 25 entities.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Page size of the request to fetch number of records matching the criteria. For example, pageSize=10 will fetch only 10 records even if there are more than 10 matching results for the query.

parameters.name: other[eq]

parameters.name: truckNumber[eq]
parameters.description: Truck number of carrier order of the shipment.

parameters.description: Tracking provider of the shipment. The operators allowed for this operand is "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, trackingProvider[in]

parameters.description: Service Area key of the LTL shipment. The operators allowed for this operand are "eq", "in". Operators are to be included within square brackets after the operand. For example, `serviceAreaKey[eq]` or `serviceAreaKey[in]`

post.description:
Create a new LTL (Less Than Truckload) rate quote request to get shipping rates from multiple sources including Banyan, Contract carriers, P44, and SMC3.

This endpoint generates rate quotes for an existing shipment by querying configured rating sources.
You can specify shipment-level services, pickup services, delivery services, and filter by service type and areas.

parameters.name: Content-Type
parameters.description: Content type of the request body

shipmentId.description:
Turvo shipment ID for which to generate rate quotes.
The shipment must already exist in Turvo with origin, destination, and freight details configured.

shipmentServices.description:
List of shipment-level services/accessories.
These are services that apply to the entire shipment.
Refer to Lookup - LTL Shipment Services for available values.

pickupServices.description:
List of pickup-specific services/accessories.
These services apply to the pickup location/process.
Refer to Lookup - LTL Pickup Services for available values.

deliveryServices.description:
List of delivery-specific services/accessories.
These services apply to the delivery location/process.
Refer to Lookup - LTL Delivery Services for available values.

segmentId.description:
Segment ID within the shipment for which to generate quotes.
If not provided, quotes will be generated for the entire shipment.

customerPricing.description:
Flag to indicate whether to apply customer-specific pricing/markup.
- true: Apply customer markup profiles and return customer-facing prices
- false: Return carrier costs without markup

sources.description:
List of rating sources to query for quotes.
If not provided, all configured sources will be queried.
Available sources:
- banyan: Banyan rating engine
- ltl-contract: Contract carrier rates
- p44: Project44 rating
- smc3-api: SMC3 API rating
- smc3: SMC3 rating

serviceType.description:
Filter quotes by service type (Standard, Expedited, Guaranteed, etc.).
Refer to Lookup - LTL Service Types for available values.

serviceAreaKeys.description:
List of service area keys to filter carriers.
Empty array means no service area filtering.
